questions.q: What real business problem does CRM software solve, per this lesson?
options: A growing company's customer and deal data stops fitting in one person's head or one spreadsheet, and needs to become a shared, structured, queryable asset
CRM exists purely to automate email marketing
CRM software is only useful for very small companies with one salesperson
CRM replaces the need for a sales team entirely
questions.explain: CRM makes customer and deal data survive any one person leaving, by making it a shared system-of-record asset.

questions.q: Why does understanding Salesforce data matter directly for an analyst's career, per this lesson?
options: Salesforce is the dominant CRM platform by market share, so it's the platform underneath an enormous share of real analyst job postings
Salesforce is a rarely-used, niche platform
Understanding Salesforce has no real career relevance
Salesforce is only used by very small startups
questions.explain: Because Salesforce dominates the CRM market, Salesforce data literacy is a widely applicable, high-value analyst skill.

questions.q: Why does this course teach the Salesforce platform and data model before teaching SOQL?
options: A query is only as good as your understanding of what you're actually querying — writing a technically correct query without understanding the data model produces meaningless numbers
SOQL is too advanced to teach early in any course
There is no real reason — it's an arbitrary ordering choice
Salesforce doesn't actually have a query language
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly warns that querying without platform understanding is how an analyst produces a technically-correct but practically meaningless number.

questions.q: What does 'Cloud' mean in a Salesforce context, per this lesson (e.g. Sales Cloud, Service Cloud)?
options: A product line built on top of Salesforce's core relational platform
A synonym for cloud computing infrastructure generally, unrelated to Salesforce products
A pricing tier available only to Enterprise customers
A deprecated legacy term no longer used by Salesforce
questions.explain: Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, and other 'Clouds' are Salesforce product lines built on its shared core data model.

questions.q: What does this course explicitly say it is NOT, per this lesson?
options: A Salesforce Administrator mega-course — it teaches exactly what a data analyst needs, not everything an admin would need
A course about CRM at all
A course intended for anyone with an analyst job title
A course that covers any query language
questions.explain: The lesson opens by explicitly distinguishing this course's scope from a full Salesforce Administrator curriculum.
